text: Developing a mobile app involves several crucial decisions. First, designers must prioritize responsive design, ensuring the interface adapts smoothly to different screen sizes and orientations. Next, developers choose between native development, which builds separate apps for iOS and Android using each platform’s specific language, or cross-platform tools like React Native, which allow one codebase to run on both systems. This choice affects cost and performance, as native apps generally offer faster, more polished interactions. Finally, the app must meet the strict guidelines of app stores like Google Play and the Apple App Store to be approved. After launch, developers constantly monitor performance, fixing bugs and releasing updates to keep users satisfied.
